label: Diagram Techniques
notes: This chapter, printed pages 227 through 246, turns tensor index notation into a projective drawing language. Open by stressing the single governing rule: an index contraction is a wire. Everything that follows, from brackets to Grassmann-Plucker relations, becomes a picture once students accept that one translation between algebra and connected legs.

label: Slots Replace Rows and Columns
notes: Explain that points and lines are both triples of numbers, distinguished only by slot variance. A point slot is outgoing, a line slot incoming, and joining opposite slots performs the incidence test. Transformations carry one in and one out slot; quadratic forms accept two incoming points. The slot bookkeeping replaces fragile row-versus-column reasoning.

label: Contraction Is a Wire
notes: Make the central abstraction concrete. A shared summation index ties two legs into one wire, and the geometry lives entirely in which slots are connected. Transposes, left versus right multiplication, and matrix order collapse into the same diagram. Encourage students to read a formula by tracing wires rather than parsing index letters.

label: Transformation Halos Cancel
notes: Under a projective matrix points map by T while lines map by the inverse transpose. Diagrammatically a halo of T sits on every outgoing point slot and an inverse halo on every incoming line slot. On an internal wire these neighbours meet and annihilate, leaving a bare identity. This is why closed invariant expressions survive coordinate change.

label: The Delta Wire
notes: Introduce the delta tensor as the invisible identity wire. Contracting delta with a vector merely relabels its index, so a delta node can always be erased or inserted on any wire. Stress the symbolic check from the notebook: the identity matrix times a vector returns the same vector, confirming delta does no geometric work.

label: The Epsilon Node and the Bracket
notes: This is the heart of the calculus. The epsilon tensor is the fully antisymmetric node with three legs in the plane. Attach three point-vectors and you contract every leg, producing the determinant bracket. Swapping any two legs flips the sign, and a repeated leg forces zero, which is exactly the collinearity condition made visual.

label: Joins and Meets
notes: Leave one epsilon leg free and the node outputs a vector instead of a scalar. Two point legs leave a line leg, giving the join as a cross product. Feed two lines and the free leg is their meet point. Emphasise that join and meet are the same epsilon node read with different free slots, exposing projective duality directly.

label: The Epsilon-Delta Rewrite
notes: Present the workhorse identity: a covariant epsilon contracted with a contravariant epsilon along one leg becomes a difference of two delta pairings. The minus sign records the crossed pairing and is never optional. Diagrammatically two three-legged nodes joined by a wire untie into a parallel pair of identity wires minus a crossed pair.

label: Meet of Two Joins
notes: Apply the rewrite to two joined point pairs. The meet of line a-b with line c-d expands into a bracket combination, and there are two equivalent splits depending on which epsilon you open first. Both land on the same intersection point. This is the diagram proof of the classical Cramer-style meet formula, verified symbolically in the notebook.

label: Grassmann-Plucker as a Picture
notes: Show that the three-term Grassmann-Plucker relation among brackets is the same epsilon-delta untying read on a different configuration. The diagram makes the symmetry transparent: rotating which legs stay closed permutes the three bracket products. Students see why the relation must hold rather than memorising a sign pattern.

label: Invariants and First Fundamental Theorem
notes: Connect to the first fundamental theorem of invariant theory: every projective invariant is a contraction of epsilon tensors with point and line vectors. A closed configuration diagram reduces to brackets and incidences, and each epsilon contributes one factor of det T under transformation, fixing the relative weight. Diagrams reveal the weight by counting epsilon nodes.

label: Recap and Practice
notes: Recap the rule set: contraction is a wire, delta is the identity wire, epsilon is the antisymmetric node, and the epsilon-delta rewrite converts networks into bracket algebra. Close with the lab discipline, attaching a numerical check to every diagram move, so a diagrammatic proof fails precisely when a local relabel, sign, or scaling check fails.
